names.note: Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 3. децембар ст. ст., „Преподобни Сава Сторожевски.“ — with «Преподобни» left off, that being the `venerable` grade `types` keeps. «Сторожевски» is the watch-hill the monastery stands on and not a rank, it is what tells him from thirty other folders whose name folds to Sabbas, and §6 asks for the fullest form the calendar gives, so the whole of the rest of the heading is the form. It is the Serbian spelling of the Russian «Савва Сторожевский» the folder already stores, one в and one Serbian suffix apart. `sr-foldpred.mjs` measured the folded string at 0 other holders, so no READ_FOLDS key is owed.

Read out of the `name:` link behind days.pravoslavie.ru’s line for 3 декабря ст. ст., name page 1904, «Преподобный Савва Сторожевский», with the rank word left off. The day’s own line adds a second epithet in brackets, «(Звенигородского)», and the life page’s first sentence prints both together, «Савва Сторожевский, Звенигородский»; the name page’s own heading is the form taken. «Сторожевский» is the hill of Storozhi, where the watch against Moscow’s enemies once stood and where he built his monastery, and it is the epithet that tells him from the twenty-odd other Sabbases in this corpus.

death.note: **Two years in three sources, and the interval holds both; it was a flat 1407 before this reading, against the folder’s own life.** Wikipedia’s article “Sabbas of Storozhi” has him die in 1407, and that is where the 1407 came from. The life printed by the Sretensky calendar (days.pravoslavie.ru) and written into this folder says he died in great old age on 3 December 1406. The Охридски пролог за 3. децембар ст. ст. closes its entry „Прешао из овог живота у бољи 1406. године“ — he passed over from this life to a better one in 1406. Two books say 1406 and one says 1407; nothing is chosen, and the basis stays attested because every one of the three states a year of its own. Two sources disagree and neither is chosen (CORPUS.md section 3). days.pravoslavie.ru’s line for 3 декабря ст. ст. brackets «(1406)» and its life closes «Скончался святой Савва в глубокой старости 3 декабря 1406 года»; the reading this folder already carried was Wikipedia’s “Sabbas of Storozhi”, a Russian monk who died in 1407. The earlier reading was recorded as `attested` from an encyclopaedia; with a calendar against it the basis drops to `traditional` and both years stand (7 October 2026).

feast.note: The second finding and translation of his relics (1998) as the Patriarchate keeps it; his principal feast is 3 December (Julian).

attestations.note: The day’s fifth entry, quoted whole with its closing full stop; URL year 2025. THE FOLDER’S OWN RUSSIAN ROW SAID THIS DAY WAS COMING: it keeps the Julian 10 August for the second finding and translation of the relics in 1998 and its note reads „his principal feast is 3 December (Julian)“, which is the day this book prints him on, so the serbian row lands on the principal feast and the russian one stays where it is. `types_add`: `wonderworker`, off «и велики чудотворац» — and a great wonderworker — where the folder held `venerable` alone; «Преподобни» is that `venerable` and «велики» is the epithet BRIEF-SERBIAN §5 keeps out of `types`. NO `abbot`: this entry does not say he was one, and the hegumenates in the folder’s life come off days.pravoslavie.ru, not off this book. `dates` WIDENED from a flat 1407 to 1406–1407, and the widening resolves an inconsistency the folder already had — its `dates` note cited Wikipedia’s 1407 while its own life, written off days.pravoslavie.ru, said he died on 3 December 1406; this book says «Прешао из овог живота у бољи 1406. године», he passed from this life to a better one in 1406. Two of the three sources now say 1406 and one says 1407; nothing is chosen. `related` UNTOUCHED: `sergius-of-radonezh` is already `related` both ways and is the only person the entry names. NO `locations`. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.

hymns.text: Пустыни явился еси доброе прозябение, преподобне,/ от юности бо изволил еси чистое житие,/ духовному твоему учителю последуя,/ и того учением ум к Небесным вперив,/ и стаду твоему премудр наставник показался еси,/ тем и Христос яко пресветла тя светильника чудесы обогати.// Савво, отче наш, моли спастися душам нашим.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 3 декабря ст. ст. — «Тропарь преподобного Саввы»

english.text: You appeared as the good shoot of the wilderness, venerable one, for from youth you chose a pure life, following your spiritual teacher and by his teaching lifting your mind to the things of heaven; and you were shown a most wise guide to your flock, and therefore Christ enriched you with wonders as a shining lamp. Savva our father, pray that our souls may be saved.

hymns.text: Господним желанием распалився,/ страсти плотския воздержанием оттряс,/ Божественнаго света незаходимое светило явился еси,/ чудес лучами всех просвещаеши,/ притекающих к мощем твоим,// Савво преподобне, отче наш.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 3 декабря ст. ст. — «Кондак преподобного Саввы»

english.text: Set alight with longing for the Lord, you shook off the passions of the flesh by abstinence and were shown an unsetting lamp of the divine light; with the rays of your wonders you enlighten all who run to your relics, venerable Savva our father.
